assistant_market_assessment.assessment_text: The observed European market is strongly segmented. Commodity/meaning-led natural-stone bead bracelets cluster roughly around €20-€100; branded fashion-jewelry gemstone bracelets frequently sit around €75-€300; a directly relevant premium natural-stone specialist (Aurum Brothers) demonstrates a credible €200-€700+ band and extends above €1,000 for rarer materials; fine-jewelry brands move quickly into €2,000-€8,000+ through precious metals and diamonds. A €599 one-of-one mineral bracelet is therefore not outside the market, but it cannot be justified by generic round-bead construction or healing-language alone. It requires visible design authorship, distinctive focal/shape/hardware composition, credible material/provenance presentation, limited/one-of-one scarcity, and premium photography/packaging/service.
assistant_market_assessment.basis_notes: Based on current public price/product examples from Aurum Brothers, Monica Vinader, AGLAIA, Bergerlin, EXODOS Copenhagen, Zolli, Shamballa Jewels and Celinni observed 2026-08-30.
implications: Closest strategic benchmark among observed brands is Aurum Brothers because it monetizes natural-stone bracelets at premium prices without relying exclusively on fine-jewelry precious-metal value.

The €599 target sits above mainstream gemstone fashion jewelry and below precious-metal fine jewelry, creating a positioning gap that must be filled by design uniqueness, material selection and storytelling rather than gemstone category alone.
Avoid competing with €20-€100 healing-stone bead bracelets on meaning claims; that segment anchors consumers to low prices and generic construction.
Use Core / Signature / One-of-One price architecture rather than forcing every design to €599; current evidence supports a premium ladder more plausibly than a single-price assortment.
One-of-one and limited small-batch language already exists in the premium natural-stone market, so uniqueness is commercially legible but is not by itself a differentiator.
